title: Scoped gate selects by file, so 265 of 1423 selected runs import the edited module but never run any of its function bodies
claim: For a diff confined to function bodies of one production file in this seat's cells, tests/closure.py:select runs every script whose closure lists the file. In 265 of the 1423 (file, script) selections over the 65 cell files, the script's traced green run (the mutation lane's own tracer) imports the file but executes no line inside any of its function bodies and never reads it as text. The selected run therefore cannot observe the edit. The worst cases are boost_drift_replay.py (341 s recorded), forced by body edits to 19 cell files it only imports; optimality.py (142.5 s) by 6; backtest, edge and validate by 7 each; and env_drift.py, by the any-integration-change belt, for 19 files its --all capture only imports. Summed recorded seconds over these pairs: 7520 s, or about 116 s per one-file body edit, before counting env_drift's stub-recorded --all run. tests/mutation_table.py already skips such pairs (never_reaches) from the same traces. closure.select does not use them.

evidence.unit: (cell file, selected script) pairs: imported, no body line executed; of 1423 selected
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, load1 ~11-13. Counts come from traces and are contention-immune. Seconds are committed recorded.seconds; env_drift/golden are costed at the measured 313 s pre-screen baseline wall, which is provisional (true)
evidence.tolerance: exact (counts); seconds provisional for env_drift/golden only

instrumented_symbol: tests/closure.py:select, against production module code objects' LINE events (tests/mutation_table.py:REACH_HOOK traces of each script's green run)
perturbation: --perturb-drop 10 removes the first 10 wasted pairs (none of them env_drift or a PRODUCERS producer) from a private closures.json patched into closure.CLOSURES: wasted_pairs 293 -> 283 and wasted_imported_pairs 265 -> 255, exactly -10 (overapprox_perturb.out). Null control --null-any-line, wasted if the run executes no line of F at all: 28 (the 21 stale entries of D3-s3-01 plus 7 env_drift belt pairs). So the body-granular excess of 265 is not file-level closure error.
metric_definition: For each production .py file F in the seat's cells and each S in closure.select([F])['run'] with a usable trace: wasted if S executes at least one line of F, no line inside any FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef body of F, and does not read F as text. Cost is S's recorded.seconds.
phenomenon_property: A script the scoped gate runs for a change can execute the changed lines. For a body-only diff, the selected script's measured reach covers at least one changed function body.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub $HOME/venv-ci/bin/python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s3/overapprox.py --json OUT lists every (file, script, seconds) wasted pair. The enumerator dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s3/enumerate.py --cells-files widens it to every production file once reach rows exist for every script
proposed_fix_scope: tests/closure.py:select: for a diff whose hunks all fall inside function bodies, skip a selected script whose recorded line reach (record it with the closure, as mutation_table.traced_baseline already does) executes none of the changed functions. Keep the file-level rule for module-level hunks, for scripts that read the file as text, and for any script without a clean reach row. The forced FULL run on main stays the backstop.
